feat(api): friendly error for stale-UTxO race on rapid re-deploy

After a deploy spends the agent's change UTxO, Blockfrost's indexer lags
~30-60s. A second deploy in that window builds against a spent input and
the node returns BadInputsUTxO. Translate that Conway error blob into a
clear 'wait and retry' message instead of surfacing raw chain internals.

S+11: recognize a peer at a distance over HTTPS (ADR-0011, Tier 6)

refactor(security+core): act on architecture/security/QA review of v0.2

A 3-agent review (architecture, security, QA) of the v0.2 remote work
surfaced real issues; this acts on the reasonable ones.

Security (the network code is the first outbound surface):
  - SSRF guard (http.ts) now parses IP literals and blocks IPv6 forms that
    EMBED a private IPv4 — IPv4-mapped (::ffff:), NAT64 (64:ff9b::), 6to4
    (2002:) — plus site-local/multicast, not just textual prefixes (H-1).
  - Redirects are followed manually (redirect:'manual') and EACH hop is
    validated before it is contacted, closing the pre-connection SSRF and
    the final-hop-only / http-downgrade gaps (H-2). DNS rebinding remains
    the sole documented residual.

Correctness:
  - propose.ts refuses a tensionAntecedent that diverges from the tension
    the staging chain already carries, so originTensionId can't record a
    provenance link the chain didn't descend from (F1).
  - resolve.ts wraps did:web percent-decoding so malformed input yields a
    diagnosable flyway error, not a raw URIError (F2).
  - localFsTransport now rejects (never throws sync) on a write failure,
    honouring its Promise contract; receipt.at is wall-clock delivery time,
    not the signed sentAt (F3, arch #2).
  - recognize.ts treats empty/whitespace locators as absent (F6).

CLI: recognize gets its own --allow-private-host flag instead of reusing
the directory-named one (arch #3 / sec M-2).

+19 tests incl. a new http.test.ts (scheme, IPv4/IPv6 ranges, H-1 bypass
addresses, H-2 redirect cases, cap boundary, timeout). Full suite 417.
New core files lint-clean; no new lint on touched legacy files.

Deferred to v0.2b (noted): DeliveryTarget.inboxRelPath and renaming the
senders' inboxPath result field — both correct for local-fs today, cheap
to revisit when github-pr adds a second transport.

feat(core+cli): S+11 — recognize a peer at a distance over HTTPS

Resolve a peer's identity from its did:web URL and recognize it with no
shared filesystem — the first fully remote flow (discover + recognize).
Closes the "recognition at a distance" gap Tier 1 left open.

core:
  - http.ts — shared, audited HTTPS fetch (assertPublicHttpsUrl +
    fetchTextOverHttps): HTTPS-only, SSRF guard (loopback/RFC-1918/link-
    local + localhost), size cap, timeout, redirect re-validation. Extracted
    from discover.ts so directory fetch and DID resolution share one path.
  - resolve.ts — didWebResolutionUrls maps did:web:github.com:owner:repo to
    its raw.githubusercontent identity artifacts (ADR-0011);
    resolvePeerIdentity fetches + id-sanity-checks them. Pre-trust: the
    crypto verification still happens in recognizePeer.
  - discover.ts now consumes http.ts (re-exports assertPublicHttpsUrl for
    compat); behavior unchanged.

cli: `flyway recognize <did:web:…> [--branch main]` resolves over HTTPS;
a non-did argument stays a local path (exactly one). Same signed
recognition entry + peer cache as local recognition — source of bytes is
invisible downstream.

+12 tests (resolve unit + remote-recognize, incl. a tamper-rejected case
proving verification still gates remote artifacts). Full suite green (398).
New files lint-clean. See ADR-0011.
